subject: Fraud & Scams
title: The OPM Hack
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The OPM Hack.

hook.text: In 2015, hackers stole security clearance files of 21.5 million U.S. government employees.

buildup.text: The Office of Personnel Management stored detailed background check data — including fingerprints.

discovery.text: The stolen files contained financial histories, mental health records, and foreign contacts.

twist.text: The breach was attributed to Chinese state hackers. It compromised U.S. intelligence for years.

climax.text: Unlike credit cards, fingerprints and personal histories cannot be changed or reissued.

punchline.text: You can change a password. You can't change a fingerprint.

quiz.question: What made the OPM breach uniquely damaging?
options: It included fingerprints and data that can't be changed
